description: Set a breakpoint at a 1-based line (and column) of a file. Name the file with `source` — a path like "src/App.tsx", or the `url` of a frame get_debugger_state or get_console_logs reported. Either way the position is mapped through source maps into the code Chrome runs, so that code must already be loaded. `url`/`urlRegex` instead take a position in the script exactly as Chrome loads it, so a source-mapped position given to them lands on the wrong line or never binds; use a frame's `compiledUrl`/`compiledLine`/`compiledColumn`. The script need not be loaded yet: an empty `resolvedLocations` means no loaded script matches yet, and the breakpoint binds when one loads — or never, if the URL is wrong. A `source` breakpoint is removed once its file changes, so set it again after an edit; the next state or navigation result lists it under `droppedBreakpoints`. A `url`/`urlRegex` breakpoint is kept through edits, so it may then stop on other code, or not at all.

condition.description: JS expression; breakpoint triggers only when truthy

source.description: File to break in, as in your project: a path like "src/App.tsx" — more of it when the name alone matches several loaded files — an absolute path, or a source-mapped url. lineNumber and columnNumber are positions in this file.

url.description: Exact URL of the script as Chrome loaded it. Provide this, urlRegex or source; if both url and urlRegex, urlRegex takes precedence.

urlRegex.description: Regex on the URL of the script as Chrome loaded it. Provide this, url or source; if both url and urlRegex, urlRegex takes precedence.

name: set_breakpoint

resolvedLocations.description: Where Chrome bound it in each loaded script, 1-based; source* give the source-mapped position. May be empty for url/urlRegex if the script is not loaded yet; the breakpoint will bind automatically when Chrome parses the script
